# Naming a USD suspense split that holds more than the invoice owes, with no
# `prepayment:` line.
#
# 120.00 arrived against 100.00 owed, so 20.00 is the customer's and has to be
# said. The overpayment refusal skipped itself wherever that account's
# currency matched the receivable's — it exists to protect a carve that reads
# the parked split's own figure, and where the currencies agree that figure is
# sound — but the carve is not the only thing at stake. Nothing else on this
# branch weighs what arrived against what is owed, so the split was moved and
# restated at 120 onto a receivable owing 100: the lot at −20, the invoice
# reading paid, and the customer's 20.00 in no credit lot, at exit 0.
#
# The `txn_guid:`-alone spelling refuses this whatever the currencies, so the
# two spellings disagreed — and the overpayment refusal's own remedy sends a
# reader to this one.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the 120.00 that arrived, the
# 100.00 owed, and the `prepayment: 20.00` that would say what the rest is.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-02
    amount: 120
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    txn_guid: "1928374655647382910abcdef0123456"
    txn_split_guid: "37465564738291a0bcdef012345678ab"
